title: quest check --continuity --base <ref>: a base-relative record-continuity check so a dropped task record cannot pass a repository green (DEC-18)
description:
DEC-18 option A (operator answer relayed first-party via opum-agent, 2026-09-29; the decision record is DEC-18 on opum-agent records): put the tracker record-continuity check in quest itself rather than copying a script into 11 repositories.

MEASURED MOTIVATION (DEC-18 context, read at opum-agent dev): each of the fleet 11 Tracker integrity jobs runs only a list parse (quest task list --json) and a managed-block currency check, so a commit that DROPS a task record passes it green. Measured instance: ward-cli b2aad11 recorded WCLI-9 as a deletion because quest task complete moved the file and only the old path was staged; the job was green on it and on the next commit. Survey 2026-09-29T06:13Z: the gap is present in 11 of 11 repositories (26 workflow files read). A record may legitimately live in any of three directories: .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive.

WHAT TO BUILD: one base-relative continuity check in quest-cli (quest check --continuity --base <ref>, or similar): it fails when an id present at the merge base resolves nowhere after the change, covering all three directories including aliases.

SCOPE AND SEQUENCING: land on dev; cut NO release. It ships in the next lore and quest pair release (Article 3); after that each repository adds one workflow line and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it. QCLI-414, the held dev promotion, stays held.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest check --continuity --base <ref> exists (shape may differ if the CLI argues for it) and reads the task ids and aliases present at the merge base of <ref> and HEAD across .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive; it exits 0 when every one of them still resolves, and it reports how many it read and resolved, so a read of zero records is itself a failure rather than a silent pass.

Red side of the two-sided proof: with a record deliberately dropped between a base and the tip (its file gone from all three directories), the check exits non-zero and NAMES the dropped id in its output; measured on a real commit pair, not asserted.

Green side of the two-sided proof: a record legitimately relocated between .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive by complete, archive or demote between the base and the tip stays green with no false positive; measured across a real commit pair in this repository where such a relocation landed.
Aliases are covered: an id reachable at the base only through an alias still counts as resolved after a relocation, and an alias that stops resolving is reported by name.

plan: 1. Add mergeBase(a, b) to the git port and LocalGitPort, so the check reads ids at the true merge base of --base and HEAD rather than at the base ref tip (a branch behind its base must not be charged for ids it never had).

2. New application service src/application/checks/continuity.ts: list the task records present at that merge base across .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive/tasks, read each one, and resolve every id and alias it declares against the current store through the same case-folded id+alias key the CLI resolves references with. Fail closed on a base read of zero records and on an unreadable record. Drafts are deliberately out of scope: draft promote removes the draft record by design, so a draft id legitimately resolves nowhere afterwards and would be a guaranteed false positive.

3. Wire quest check --continuity --base <ref> through the manifest, help and dispatch. Broken continuity is drift on exit 6 naming every missing reference in `input`; an unresolvable --base ref is not_found, and a base with no records or an unreadable one is validation.

4. Tests: two-sided proof over real commits in temp workspaces (a deliberate drop goes red and names the id; complete, archive and demote relocations stay green), alias coverage both ways (a dotted alias still resolves after a relocation; a vanished alias is reported), and the zero-read refusal. Then the real-pair measurement runs against this repository own history.
5. Full suite under the pinned bun 1.4.2 PATH prefix; land via a PR to dev; cut NO release.
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED (dev-bound). Shape: a new `check` command family with `--continuity` required rather than implied (the fleet copies one line into each CI job, so a bare `check` silently meaning continuity would make a second check a breaking change), a new GitPort.mergeBase so the comparison is against the merge base -- a branch behind its base is never charged for ids it never had -- and src/application/checks/continuity.ts, which reads the base tree through the git port and resolves against the same all-locations listing every other command uses.

FAIL-CLOSED DECISIONS, each pinned by a test. (a) A base read of zero records is a failure, not a silent pass: `listFiles` answers [] both for an empty tree and for a listing Git refused, so a zero read cannot be told apart from a wrong --base, and passing then would be the same false green this check exists to remove. (b) An unreadable record fails the check rather than narrowing its own population -- a record the check could not read is one whose disappearance it could not report. (c) Drafts are deliberately OUT of the population in both directions: `draft promote` removes the draft record by design while minting a task under a NEW id, so including draft ids would make every promotion a guaranteed false positive. That one was found by reading promoteDraft, not by a failing test -- it would have gone red on the first real promotion.

TWO-SIDED PROOF over real Git commits (9 tests, test/qcli415-record-continuity.test.ts): complete, archive and demote relocations between base and tip stay green; a deliberately dropped record goes red on exit 6 and names the id in the message (not only in a structured field); an id reachable only through an alias still resolves after a relocation; an alias that stops resolving is reported by name; a base with no records is exit 6 validation; an unresolvable --base is exit 3 not_found; and a branch behind its base is not charged for ids added to the base after the branch point.

LOCALISATION, by mutating the CHECK rather than its input -- three mutations, each reddening exactly the predicted single test and nothing else: read the base ref instead of the merge base (only the merge-base case red), ignore the aliases list (only the vanished-alias case red -- and note the alias-GREEN test stayed green under this mutation, which is why both alias directions exist), and drop the zero-read guard (only the zero-read case red). Each mutation was reverted before the green run.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, real history, not a fixture: from origin/main 412 records and 671 references (ids plus aliases) all resolving; from the initial commit a9fbc78a, 521 of 521 resolving -- 259 more references than records, which is the migration alias set (dotted ids and backlog: provenance aliases) surviving the renumbering. Red direction on real records: a scratch commit that removed QCLI-101 from the working tree made the check exit 6 with "2 of 673 references ... resolve to no task record: QCLI-101, backlog:/Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli:active:QCLI-101" -- both spellings of the dropped record named, which is AC4 holding on real data rather than on a fixture. The scratch commit was discarded; nothing was pushed from it.

COST, named so nobody has to measure it twice: the base side reads one blob per record sequentially (about 2 seconds for this repository 414 records). Deterministic order is why the missing list comes out in base order; a batch read is a contained follow-up if a CI budget ever objects.

SUITE: full `bun run check` green under the pinned bun 1.4.2 -- 1014 pass, 0 fail, 115 files (the 9 here are the delta from 1005). No release, per DEC-18: this ships in the next lore and quest pair release, after which each repository adds one workflow line and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it.

Written AFTER that request, so it is the note a successor should restore from. Everything below was measured or verified live, not inferred.

finalSummary:
LANDED on dev as 9c0b7bd8 (opum-ai/quest-cli#429, squash, required contexts green on head 4f07ce34). No release, per DEC-18: this ships in the next lore and quest pair release, after which each repository adds one workflow line and opum-cli-e2e qualifies it. dev is one commit ahead of main, unpromoted; that promotion is the orchestrator call, not this task own.

WHAT LANDED: a new `check` command family -- `quest check --continuity --base <ref>` fails when a task record id or alias present at the merge base of <ref> and HEAD resolves to no record in the current store. It reads .quest/tasks, .quest/completed and .quest/archive/tasks at the base through a new GitPort.mergeBase, and resolves against the same all-locations listing every other command uses. `--continuity` is required rather than implied, because the fleet copies one line into each CI job.

AC1, measured: the command exists and reports its counts (records, references, resolved, missing). Real runs on this repository: from origin/main 412 records and 671 references all resolving; from the initial commit a9fbc78a, 521 of 521 (the 259 extra references are the migration aliases); after landing, from base 835043e2, 413 records and 672 references all resolving. A base read of zero records is exit 6, not a pass -- the positive control, pinned by its own test.

AC2, measured on a real commit pair: a scratch commit removing QCLI-101 from the working tree made the check exit 6 with "Record continuity: 2 of 673 references present at the merge base ... resolve to no task record: QCLI-101, backlog:/Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli:active:QCLI-101" -- the id named in the message, not only in the structured field. The scratch commit was discarded and never left this checkout. The same shape is asserted in the test file over temp repositories with real commits.

AC3, measured on a real commit pair in this repository where relocations landed: base 835043e2 against landed dev, between which QCLI-413 and QCLI-414 moved from .quest/tasks to .quest/completed, exits 0 with every reference resolving. The test file loops complete, archive and demote as separate real-commit cases.

AC4, measured both ways: an id reachable only through an alias still resolves after a relocation (test), a vanished alias is reported by name (test), and the real red run above named both the dropped id and its backlog: provenance alias, which is the alias machinery exercised on real data rather than a fixture.

LOCALISATION, by mutating the check rather than its input: read the base ref instead of the merge base; ignore the aliases list; drop the zero-read guard. Each mutation reddened exactly the predicted single test (8 pass / 1 fail each), and the alias-GREEN test correctly stayed green under the alias mutation -- which is why both alias directions exist. Mutations reverted before the green run; the full local suite is 1014 pass / 0 fail under the pinned bun 1.4.2.

FAIL-CLOSED DECISIONS, each pinned: zero records read at the base is a failure; an unreadable record fails the check rather than narrowing its own population; drafts are out of scope in both directions because `draft promote` removes the draft record by design while minting a new id -- including draft ids would make every promotion a false positive (found by reading promoteDraft, not by a failing test).

COST, named for the CI consumer: the base side reads one blob per record sequentially, about 2 seconds at this repository 414 records; order is deterministic so `missing` comes out in base order. A batch read is a contained follow-up if a CI budget ever objects.
